app.title: HEEH-V1™ DICOM Viewer
app.summary: A person loads a study by choosing a folder, uploading files or ZIPs, or giving a TCIA manifest. Earlier exports are recognised, and their measurements come back with them. They move through images and slices, set the display window, and point at the image to read calibrated pixel values. They click points to draw labelled distance and angle measurements, click a spot to inspect a region of interest, and turn on intensity, quality, radiomics and CT metric calculations shown in result tabs. They can browse by series and set a second image beside the first, then export de-identified DICOM, a structured report, measurement CSV/JSON, radiomics tables, an annotated PNG and an HTML research report in one validated package.

task.text: Take calibrated measurements and quantitative features from medical images and export them, de-identified and with provenance, for research.

data.text: Medical image studies (DICOM, NIfTI, NRRD, MetaImage or raster) as single images, multi-frame volumes or series, with header metadata such as pixel spacing and rescale values
data.item: one image or slice of a medical image series

stage.text: measuring and computing features on acquired scans, before reporting them

mechanism.text: A sidebar picks the input, display window and which analyses to run. A large canvas shows the selected slice at native scale, reports the calibrated value under the pointer, and takes clicks for distance, angle and ROI measurements, which are drawn as coloured rulers and listed in a panel next to it. Computed results appear in tabs under the image, a collapsible area holds series selection and a side-by-side comparison, and a single export dialog packages everything with a manifest.

field.text: calibrated image measurement and radiomics on CT and MR in medical imaging research

workflow.name: measure features on images and export the measurements

steps.here: Local directory path or direct upload of DICOM, NIfTI, NRRD, MHA, raster or ZIP files, or a TCIA manifest. Slices are put in physical order and earlier exports have their measurements restored.

steps.step: step through items one at a time
steps.here: Previous/Next buttons, an image-index slider and a slice-position slider for volumes, plus a series selector.

steps.step: adjust how each item is displayed
steps.here: CT window presets (lung, bone, brain, and so on) with center and width sliders in HU, plus 1:1, 2x or 4x magnification. These change only the display and leave the source pixels alone.

steps.step: mark points on an item to measure it
steps.here: In Distance mode, two clicks; in Angle mode, three clicks with the vertex first. Values are in mm, cm, px or deg from DICOM PixelSpacing or a manual mm/pixel factor. Each measurement gets a label, a colour and a line-intensity profile, and can be deleted, undone or cleared.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Checkboxes for tissue classification, edge maps, image quality and radiomics (with an optional IBSI ROI mask). Results show in Intensity, Quality, Radiomics, Volume and CT Metrics tabs.
A 'Compare side-by-side' selector puts another image next to the current one, using the same window settings.
An Export dialog offers de-identified DICOM, DICOM SR, measurement CSV/JSON, annotated PNG, radiomics CSV/XLSX, cohort CSV, an HTML report, or a ZIP of everything with a SHA-256 manifest.

distinctive: Measurements are stored in source-pixel coordinates and converted to physical units with per-axis DICOM pixel spacing. Display windowing never changes the values that get measured.
Exports are de-identified, with pseudonymous filenames and remapped UIDs, and a manifest of hashes is checked before download.
Earlier exports (JSON, PNG metadata, DICOM SR) can be loaded again, and their measurements come back onto the matching image.
The tools on offer depend on the detected modality and SOP class. For example, CT windowing and HU metrics appear only for CT.
